summary: Readout from post-incident bridge: Silvergate experienced a multi-region inference surge causing elevated tail latency and partial fallback to smaller model variants. Redwood provided initial mitigation (fallback routing and temporary reservation). Discussion focused on root cause (unexpected burst pattern + cold KV cache + kernel fallback on quantized paths), agreed next steps for trace sharing, a controlled re-run, and SLA amendment language for burst shielding.
topics: incident timeline and root cause hypotheses
fallback and routing behavior during surge
KV cache warmup and prefill strategies
transcript: [00:00] Jordan (Redwood): good afternoon everyone i think we can get started thanks for making time, this is the silvergate readout, um quick agenda: timeline, root cause guesses, mitigation recap, and next steps

[00:18] Tomás (Silvergate): yeah thanks Jordan, appreciate it. morning for us — we saw a big spike friday night, about 45 minutes where p99 blew out, users hit re-tries and then the app fell back to cached results

[00:34] Maya (SRE): yeah the app logs show a spike in request rate to the text-generation endpoint, about 6x baseline, CPU on the orchestrator was fine but GPUs started queuing, we saw queuing time increase and then some requests were routed to a smaller model variant
[00:50] Priya (Redwood SE): okay so a couple quick clarifiers — when you say routed to smaller model, was that our automatic fallback or a manual route?
[00:58] Connor (Silvergate): that was automatic, we have a policy to fall back after 800ms. i think there was a throughput limiter that fired too late

[01:10] Priya (Redwood SE): got it. initial telemetry we saw matches: high concurrency, KV cache cold for many new prefixes from the campaign, and some kernel selection fell back to the slower quantized path under memory pressure — there's a couple of small transcription notes, by the way, some labels might be off in the bundle
[01:35] Rita (Security): before we go deep i just want to confirm what data was touched during the incident; were any prompts or outputs persisted outside your primary VPC?
[01:44] Luis (CSM): short answer no, Silvergate stayed within its dedicated capacity, fallback models were still in the same tenancy — we can supply the audit logs and retention traces
[01:58] Maya (SRE): we did see increased egress to our caching layer, but nothing left the VPC. can you include the KMS key use in the trace? we'll need that for compliance
[02:12] Priya (Redwood SE): absolutely we'll include KMS usage, key IDs may be redacted but we can show the envelope operations and timestamps. we'll also annotate which replica handled each request

[02:29] Jordan (Redwood AE): i want to walk the timeline quickly: 23:04 spike starts, 23:08 queue depth increases, 23:12 fallback triggers on ~12% of in-flight requests, 23:15 auto-reserve activated to add capacity in eu-west-1 but it came up after the busiest window
[02:50] Tomás (Silvergate): so timing mismatch — autoscale lag was the painful part. is that because of image pull or just provisioning?

[03:00] Priya (Redwood SE): a mix — provisioning plus kernel warmup and model load time. we also saw some requests hit a quantized execution path due to memory pressure which is slightly slower for long sequences, that contributed to p99
[03:20] Maya (SRE): the KV cache hit rate was awful for the campaign because of lots of new user prompts — was there any prefetching we could have enabled?
[03:31] Priya (Redwood SE): there is a prefill recommendation we pushed but it wasn't enabled; we can show the default prefill window we suggest for high-cardinality prefix patterns
[03:46] Jordan (Redwood AE): and that prefill ties into our caching docs — we should send the config diff next step, that's one of the quick wins
[03:55] Tomás (Silvergate): quick win is great but we need guarantee on SLA, the business impact was material. we need a contractual protection against these burst scenarios

[04:06] Luis (CSM): understood. we're going to propose an addendum that covers burst shielding, a short buffer of reservation plus a priority lane to reduce tail exposure — i'll draft an initial delta
[04:20] Rita (Security): from a security perspective we also need the SOC2 report and the encryption key rotation history around the incident window
[04:29] Priya (Redwood SE): we'll include SOC2 scope and HSM/KMS ops, note that some of our private deployments have different rotation cadence; i'll annotate which environment is which
[04:43] Maya (SRE): can you also include the raw producer traces? our SREs want flamegraphs, per-token timing, and the kernel selectors that were active

[04:53] Priya (Redwood SE): yes that's in the support bundle — traces, kernel logs, VM/GPU perf counters. warning: transcription may swap kv with k v or k dash v in the file names, so ignore slight name mismatches
[05:07] Tomás (Silvergate): one hypothesis — we think an upstream campaign changed prompt shapes and caused many long sequences at once. did you see a shift in seq length distribution?
[05:17] Priya (Redwood SE): we did, median stayed similar but p95/p99 sequence length rose sharply, that interacts poorly with batching heuristics leading to head-of-line blocking in some bins
[05:30] Connor (Silvergate): so batching heuristics — can we force a different policy during bursts? like smaller batch max or emergency prioritization for business-critical routes?
[05:40] Priya (Redwood SE): yes we have routing policies you can pin to a dedicated pool or lower batch sizes for critical endpoints, the tradeoff is higher per-token cost but lower tail latency
[05:53] Maya (SRE): cost tradeoffs are fine if we get SLA guarantees. Tomás: do we want dedicated capacity?
[06:02] Tomás (Silvergate): expensive long term for us. we prefer a hybrid: reserved baseline plus burst shielding via on-demand warm standbys and prefill for new prefixes
[06:14] Jordan (Redwood AE): that map makes sense, we'll put together a recommended configuration: baseline reservation + warm pool + prefill + emergency routing. Luis will attach pricing
[06:28] Rita (Security): also timeline on artifact delivery, we need docs within 72 hours for our auditors
[06:35] Luis (CSM): we can get the initial support bundle out within 4 business days, i'll push for quicker; Priya will own the traces
[06:45] Priya (Redwood SE): yes, support bundle with traces and per-request annotations by 2027-01-04, note there may be scrubbed fields for PII per the agreement
[06:55] Tomás (Silvergate): one technical ask — can Redwood annotate which requests hit quantized paths vs native kernels so we can correlate to latency spikes?
[07:08] Priya (Redwood SE): yes we tag kernel decisions in the trace; sometimes the label is 'qpath' or 'int8-path' and transcription might label it weirdly, but it's there
[07:20] Maya (SRE): i'd like a short-run test where you replay the captured traffic against a staging cluster and we compare p50/p95/p99 and tail heatmaps
[07:30] Jordan (Redwood AE): we'll schedule a controlled replay; Jordan to own scheduling, Priya to own the cluster setup. we'll run both warm and cold cache cases
[07:42] Connor (Silvergate): during replay can you force the autoscale latency so we test the slow path?
[07:48] Priya (Redwood SE): yes we can throttle the control plane to emulate provisioning lag; we'll also simulate model-load times to capture warmup cost
[07:58] Tomás (Silvergate): on the SLA amendment, we need a clause that accounts for 'burst exposure' with defined remediation and credit if fallback exceeds x%
[08:10] Luis (CSM): we'll propose a tiered credit model tied to percent of traffic hitting fallback and duration — also include an operations runbook for immediate mitigation
[08:22] Rita (Security): small security note: please ensure the replays are done in a staging VPC with redacted PII, we will not allow real card data in a test cluster
[08:33] Priya (Redwood SE): agreed, replay will use tokenized placeholders. we'll also provide a scrubbed sample of prompts for function testing

[08:45] Jordan (Redwood AE): ok let's talk about immediate mitigations applied Friday: a temporary reservation, forced priority lane for customer routes, and raising rate limits on the warm pool — that stabilized things after about 10 minutes
[09:02] Maya (SRE): roughly 10 minutes — but the business impact window was the first 6 minutes with many retries. we want better than 10 minute containment
[09:13] Priya (Redwood SE): understood. operationally we can reduce model load time by preloading the most-used model shards and keep a minimal warm pool always hot for pinned customers
[09:26] Tomás (Silvergate): cost delta for always-hot pool?
[09:31] Luis (CSM): i'll include conservative numbers in the SLA delta, plus an option for on-demand warm-up credits so you only pay when we actually reserve
[09:42] Connor (Silvergate): also can we get a dashboard for prefix cardinality so our product team can see if a campaign will produce many new prefixes?
[09:51] Priya (Redwood SE): yes we can provide a prefix-cardinality dashboard and alerting thresholds, we'll include it in the operational playbook
[10:00] Tomás (Silvergate): great, that helps product too. any other questions from security?
[10:06] Rita (Security): just to clarify retention on traces: how long will Redwood keep the raw perf traces? we need them for audit trail
[10:14] Priya (Redwood SE): default retention 90 days for support traces unless you request longer; we can arrange extended retention with an addendum
[10:24] Maya (SRE): could we set up automatic prefills for campaigns identified as high-cardinality?
[10:31] Priya (Redwood SE): yes we can add a campaign flag and a prefill policy; we'll document the API calls for the product team

[10:40] Jordan (Redwood AE): ok recap and owners: Priya sends support bundle and kernel logs by jan 4; Jordan schedules replay by jan 6; Luis drafts SLA amendment by jan 10; Maya sends traffic sample jan 5
[10:58] Tomás (Silvergate): thanks — please include an executive note we can forward to our GRC team summarizing the mitigation and timeline
[11:06] Luis (CSM): will do, i'll draft an executive summary after the replay results
[11:12] Rita (Security): quick ask — include the KMS rotation audit you discussed earlier in the bundle
[11:20] Priya (Redwood SE): noted. we'll include KMS envelope logs and rotation summary
[11:28] Maya (SRE): last thing: can Redwood include a short runbook snippet we can embed in our ops page for immediate mitigation steps?
[11:36] Jordan (Redwood AE): yes, we'll include a one-page runbook with commands to pin routing, increase warm pool, and enable smaller batch policy
[11:45] Tomás (Silvergate): perfect. timeline looks reasonable. we'll reconvene after the replay results
[11:50] Jordan (Redwood AE): thanks everyone. leaving open items in the action list and i'll send calendar invite for replay window. meeting adjourned
[11:57] (background): brief crosstalk and hangups — some participants still asking about kernel labels (garbled), audio dropouts at 12:03
